Quotes his own 10-year extension ([[2026-10-28-margincall4-breakout-10y-tsla-extension]]) and answers the question "Is this algo strategy an overfitted POS?" with **No** — backed by a three-measure validation table (OCR-recovered from chart, 1338×432, preserved at `rdp_media/2115500833509188057/chart.png`).

## Summary

The author stress-tests the 10-year QQQ/TSLA/BTC breakout portfolio against the three standard overfitting batteries:

| Measure | What it is | Usual pass mark | Ours |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Deflated Sharpe ratio** (Bailey & López de Prado) — most cited in quant finance | probability the Sharpe survives multiple-testing deflation | > 0.95 | **0.9998** |
| **Probability of Backtest Overfitting** (PBO), t-score after multiple testing (Harvey & Liu) — "closest to what you asked" | share of resamples where the in-sample best underperforms out-of-sample; t after multiple-testing haircut | PBO under 10–20%; over 50% = overfit · t > 3 | **PBO 0.7%** · **t 2.9 strict, 3.7 at 1,000 tries** |
| **Walk-forward test** — what most practitioners actually use | re-fit/evaluate on rolling out-of-sample windows | keeps > 50–60% of backtest return OOS | **keeps ~70–80% (38%/yr vs 49.5%/yr backtest)** |
